I did what was asked of me in this message. I increased the ram available to iGPU.  I didn't see the other options: """TurboQuant / Strix Halo plan — Phase 0a action list
Plan file: .claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md
Worktree: .claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker
Committed so far: 5bcae51a0 (Phases 0-2), 4f2f0b2bc (BIOS probe)

================================================================
CURRENT STATE (from scripts/check_bios_state.py, 2026-04-18)
================================================================
  [OK]  GPU target: gfx1151 detected
  [OK]  CPU features: AVX-512 / VNNI / BF16 present (AMD Zen 5)
  [OK]  User groups: render, video already present
  [OK]  ROCm 7.2.1 installed (want 7.2.2)

  [--]  Kernel: 6.17.0-1017-oem  (need 6.18.4+)
  [--]  VRAM allocation: 0.5 GB  (BIOS UMA is not set to Auto; blocks
everything)
  [--]  PCIe link speed: unknown without sudo

The 0.5 GB VRAM reading is the headline. No amount of kernel / ROCm / software
work can exceed the BIOS UMA cap. BIOS visit MUST come first.

================================================================
STEP 1 — BIOS (physical, you only)
================================================================
1. Save any work, reboot.
2. At POST, press F2 / F12 / Del (Framework Desktop defaults to F2) to
enter setup.
3. Locate and set:
     - UMA Frame Buffer      -> Auto
     - AI Max Performance    -> Enabled
     - PCIe Speed            -> Gen5
4. Save & Exit. Let the machine boot into Linux normally.
5. Log in.

================================================================
STEP 2 — Confirm BIOS took effect (no sudo)
================================================================
  cd ~/dev/cohezion/.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker
  .venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py

Expected change: VRAM row should now report >= ~100 GB. If it still reads
low, the BIOS change didn't stick — revisit BIOS before continuing.

================================================================
STEP 3 — Resume automated work with Claude
================================================================
Start a new Claude Code session in the worktree and send this prompt:

  continue the turboquant plan from Phase 0a step 6 — BIOS is done,
  paste the probe output below and proceed:

  <paste the output of the scripts/check_bios_state.py run from Step 2>

I will then:
  - Verify VRAM is now large (confirms BIOS)
  - Drive kernel 6.17 -> 6.18.4 upgrade (direct .deb from kernel.ubuntu.com,
    no Mainline GUI needed; sudo password prompts as we go)
  - Refresh AMDGPU strix_halo* firmware blobs
  - Upgrade ROCm 7.2.1 -> 7.2.2
  - Reboot between steps as required
  - Re-probe after each reboot

Each sudo command will prompt interactively for your password — I will not
store or cache it, per the project security rule.

================================================================
STEP 4 — After Phase 0a greens, I proceed (no more sudo needed)
================================================================
  - Phase 0b: install vllm-rocm nightly in scratch venv, build stock
    llama.cpp + Vulkan RADV, run backend bake-off probe.
  - Phase 3: launchers for vLLM on :13308 and llama.cpp PR #20969 on
    :13307 (the real TurboQuant unlock).
  - Phase 4: AMD Quark QuaRot offline conversion of Gemma-4-E2B for NPU.
  - Phase 5: n>=20 benchmarks populate registry.py and SHOWCASE.md.

================================================================
WHAT I CAN NOT DO
================================================================
  - Change BIOS settings (no OS-side API on Framework Desktop).
  - Press the power button if a kernel hangs on boot (rare, but worth
    being near the machine during Phase 0a reboots).
  - Set a password for passwordless sudo (you chose interactive mode).

That's it. Any command I would otherwise type myself is in the steps above.
"""

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

---BIOS INSTRUCTIONS---
# TurboQuant / Strix Halo — Phase 0a Action List

**Plan file:** `.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md`
**Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker`
**Committed so far:** `5bcae51a0` (Phases 0-2), `4f2f0b2bc` (BIOS probe)

## Current state (from `scripts/check_bios_state.py`, 2026-04-18)

- [OK]  GPU target: gfx1151 detected
- [OK]  CPU features: AVX-512 / VNNI / BF16 present (AMD Zen 5)
- [OK]  User groups: render, video already present
- [OK]  ROCm 7.2.1 installed (want 7.2.2)
- [--]  Kernel: 6.17.0-1017-oem  (need 6.18.4+)
- [--]  VRAM allocation: **0.5 GB**  (BIOS UMA is not set to Auto; blocks everything)
- [--]  PCIe link speed: unknown without sudo

The 0.5 GB VRAM reading is the headline. No amount of kernel / ROCm / software
work can exceed the BIOS UMA cap. BIOS visit MUST come first.

## Step 1 — BIOS (physical, you only)

1. Save any work, reboot.
2. At POST, press F2 / F12 / Del (Framework Desktop defaults to F2) to enter setup.
3. Locate and set:
   - UMA Frame Buffer      → Auto
   - AI Max Performance    → Enabled
   - PCIe Speed            → Gen5
4. Save & Exit. Let the machine boot into Linux normally.
5. Log in.

## Step 2 — Confirm BIOS took effect (no sudo)

```bash
cd ~/dev/cohezion/.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py
```

Expected change: VRAM row should now report ≥ ~100 GB. If it still reads low,
the BIOS change didn't stick — revisit BIOS before continuing.

## Step 3 — Resume automated work with Claude

Start a new Claude Code session in the worktree and send this prompt:

> continue the turboquant plan from Phase 0a step 6 — BIOS is done, paste the
> probe output below and proceed:
>
> `<paste the output of the scripts/check_bios_state.py run from Step 2>`

I will then:
- Verify VRAM is now large (confirms BIOS)
- Drive kernel 6.17 → 6.18.4 upgrade (direct `.deb` from kernel.ubuntu.com, no Mainline GUI needed; sudo password prompts as we go)
- Refresh AMDGPU `strix_halo*` firmware blobs
- Upgrade ROCm 7.2.1 → 7.2.2
- Reboot between steps as required
- Re-probe after each reboot

Each sudo command will prompt interactively for your password — I will not
store or cache it, per the project security rule.

# Unlock TurboQuant for Strix Halo Local Inference

**Plan created:** 2026-04-18
**Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker`
**Scope:** Wire real ICLR 2026 TurboQuant KV-cache compression into `cohezion.inference`
across all three Strix Halo compute engines (iGPU/NPU/CPU), producing measurable
throughput and long-context gains with honest benchmarks.

---

## Context

**Why this plan exists:** `cohezion.inference` already references TurboQuant in
six places (`registry.py:102,129`, `fleet.py:14,107-123`, `__init__.py:27-28`,
`SHOWCASE.md`, `MANIFEST_ALIGNMENT.md`), but the feature is non-functional today:

1. `fleet._inject_symmetry_axis()` tries to import `cohezion.core.symmetry_hardware_bridge` — **that file does not exist**. The ImportError is caught and logged at DEBUG level, so every `route()` call runs with an unmodified payload. Silent failure in production (violates CLAUDE.md Learning 359).
2. `ModelEntry.quantization: str` conflates weight quant and KV quant (e.g. `"INT4+turboquant"`). Per the ICLR 2026 paper, TurboQuant is **KV-cache only** — it must be separable from weight quant.
3. `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` is referenced in CLAUDE.md but **does not exist** at repo root. No single source of truth for gfx1151 / XDNA 2 / Zen 5 capabilities.
4. Latency fields in `registry.py:109-112` are `None`. Only informal 5-call warm observations exist in `SHOWCASE.md` — not statistically valid per the in-file comment.

**Target outcome:** TurboQuant KV compression actually flowing end-to-end on
the iGPU lane (6× KV memory reduction → fits 70B at 128k context in unified
memory), NPU lane using AMD Quark QuaRot weight rotation (nearest prior art
since AMD compiler has no TurboQuant operator yet), CPU lane honestly marked
as R&D, and reproducible `n≥20` benchmarks replacing the informal numbers.

---

## Research summary (URLs embedded for audit)

Two data streams were combined: (A) web agent research on April 18, (B) two Gemini
guidance PDFs supplied by the user from Apr 17–18, 2026. Where they disagree, the
plan takes **both paths in parallel** and lets Phase 0b's probe decide.

- **Paper:** TurboQuant (Zandieh et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv:2504.19874). Two-stage: PolarQuant (Hadamard rotation → Lloyd-Max scalar quant) + QJL 1-bit residual. Data-free, training-free, online. 3.5-bit achieves FP16 parity, 6× KV compression on Llama-3.1-70B @ 128k.
- **Runtime integration landscape (Apr 17–18 PDFs):**
  - **vLLM-rocm nightly** (ROCm 7.2 wheels): `--kv-cache-dtype tbq4` flag; PDF calls this the "maximum path" for Strix Halo agentic workloads.
  - **Upstream `llama.cpp` PR #20969** ("turboquant-exp" branch): `--kv-cache-type turbo3|tq4`, built with `GGML_HIP=1 AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1150` (alias of gfx1151).
  - **SGLang PR #21617**: Triton-backed integration, ideal for high-throughput serving.
  - `turboquant-torch` (PyPI v0.2.0) retained as correctness oracle only.
- **Strix Halo state — source conflict:**
  - Web research (community benchmarks, ROCm#6146): pre-7.2.x ROCm had a >64GB VRAM load bug on gfx1151; Vulkan RADV measured 36.8 t/s and was the recommended backend.
  - PDFs (Apr 18): **ROCm 7.2.2** is the first release with *stable* TurboQuant support on RDNA 3.5; kernel 6.18.4 + AMDGPU firmware blobs required; `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.0`; UMA dynamically scales to ~112 GB on 6.18.4 (up from 96 GB BIOS cap).
  - **Plan posture:** Phase 0b builds a probe that exercises both ROCm 7.2.2 and Vulkan RADV stacks on the same model; whichever completes a 32k-token pass without crash or quality loss becomes primary for Phase 3. Do NOT assume.
- **Ryzen AI SW 1.7.1 (Apr 8, NPU lane):** INT4 native, MXFP4 converts to INT4, no TurboQuant operator yet. Unchanged by the PDFs.
- **AMD Quark 0.10** ships QuaRot (rotation-based weight quant, same family as TurboQuant). Complementary to KV-side TurboQuant; used in Phase 4.
- **No AVX-512 TurboQuant kernels exist.** CPU lane gets no KV compression this cycle.

---

## Design decisions (user-confirmed)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scope | Full KV-cache TurboQuant per ICLR 2026 paper |
| Hardware targets | iGPU (Vulkan RADV) primary + NPU (Ryzen AI 1.7.1) + CPU (future) |
| Implementation strategy | Four-layer: torch = ground truth oracle; **vLLM-rocm (ROCm 7.2.2) primary**; **upstream llama.cpp PR #20969 secondary**; **SGLang PR #21617 tertiary**; Vulkan RADV on stock llama.cpp as documented fallback if ROCm 7.2.2 regresses. |
| Research stash | Audit-then-merge if found (current stash is BMAD housekeeping, not turboquant research — start fresh) |
| Source-of-truth when PDF and web-research disagree | Empirical probe in Phase 0b decides; no assumption locked in until a 32k-token round-trip succeeds. |

---

## Phased approach

### Phase 0a — Kernel / firmware / BIOS prep (OUT-OF-BAND, user-gated)

**Goal:** Bring the host up to the April 2026 baseline the Gemini PDF prescribes.
Every step here is destructive/reversible-with-care, so each is a user confirmation
point — the agent does **not** run these unattended.

- **Kernel 6.18.4** via Mainline (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS host):
  ```bash
  sudo add-apt-repository ppa:cappelikan/ppa -y
  sudo apt update && sudo apt install mainline -y
  # Then: open Mainline, select 6.18.4, Install, reboot.
  uname -r   # must print 6.18.4 or later
  ```
- **AMDGPU firmware refresh** (strix_halo* blobs from linux-firmware):
  ```bash
  git clone https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git
  cd linux-firmware/amdgpu
  sudo cp strix_halo* /lib/firmware/amdgpu/
  sudo update-initramfs -u && sudo reboot
  ```
- **BIOS (Framework v3.05 or later):** UMA Frame Buffer = **Auto**, AI Max Performance Mode = **Enabled**, PCIe = **Gen5**. Document values actually set in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md`.
- **Environment pin** (goes into `~/.cohezion/strix_halo.env`, sourced by launcher scripts):
  ```bash
  export HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.0
  export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
  export GPU_MAX_WORKGROUP_SIZE=1024
  export AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151
  export ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm
  export PATH="/opt/rocm/bin:$PATH"
  ```
  Note: `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` is **11.5.0** per the Apr 17 PDF, not 11.5.1 (currently in `SHOWCASE.md` — to be corrected in Phase 5).

**Verification gate (non-destructive probe):**
```bash
uname -r                         # 6.18.4+
rocminfo | grep gfx1151          # device present
dmesg | grep -i 'strix_halo'     # firmware loaded
rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram      # ≥ ~108 GB reported on Auto UMA
```

**Deliverable:** host at the baseline the stack requires. Nothing in `src/` changes here.

---

### Phase 0b — Runtime probe (ROCm 7.2.2 vs Vulkan RADV bake-off)

**Goal:** Resolve the source conflict empirically. Do **not** commit to a
primary backend until we have numbers.

- Install ROCm 7.2.2 repo + `rocm-hip-sdk rocm-visual-confirm` per PDF.
- Install `vllm-rocm` nightly in a scratch venv:
  ```bash
  uv venv ~/.venvs/tbq_probe
  . ~/.venvs/tbq_probe/bin/activate
  uv pip install --pre vllm-rocm --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/rocm7.2
  ```
- Install a Vulkan-RADV stock-`llama.cpp` build as control arm.
- Run `scripts/probe_backend.py` (new, < 120 lines) that executes:
  1. `vllm serve unsloth/Llama-3.5-70B-Q4_K_M --kv-cache-dtype tbq4 --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enforce-eager --device cuda` then a 32k prompt.
  2. Same prompt against stock llama.cpp + Vulkan RADV (no TBQ).
- Record: did ROCm path OOM / crash on >64GB load? Peak VRAM used, TTFT, tokens/sec.
- Write `benchmarks/backend_probe_2026-04-18.md` with the outcome and a **clear recommendation** — this becomes the input to Phase 3.

**Deliverable:** evidence-grounded choice between ROCm 7.2.2 and Vulkan fallback.

---

### Phase 0 — Foundation (unblock silent failures)

**Goal:** Stop the silent `ImportError`, establish the missing reference docs.

- **Create** `src/cohezion/core/symmetry_hardware_bridge.py` with a minimal real `get_symmetry_bridge()` + `SymmetryHardwareBridge.apply_to_payload()`. For Phase 0 it returns the payload with a `turboquant_axis: {coherence, hadamard_seed, bits}` dict appended — downstream runtimes ignore unknown fields today, enabling the full wiring before Lemonade/llama.cpp parse it.
- **Tighten** `fleet._inject_symmetry_axis` (`fleet.py:107-123`): keep the narrow except tuple, but raise `logger.warning` (not debug) if the bridge returns None; add a once-per-process `RuntimeError` check when `COHEZION_STRICT_AXIS=1` is set so tests can catch regressions.
- **Create** `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` at repo root documenting Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (gfx1151), XDNA 2 (50 TOPS), Radeon 8060S (40 CU, 256 GB/s), 128 GB LPDDR5X, Ryzen AI SW 1.7.1 pin, ROCm>64GB bug, Vulkan RADV preference.
- **Tests:** `tests/inference/test_symmetry_bridge.py` — import, apply_to_payload adds expected keys, strict mode raises on bridge-missing.

**Deliverable:** every `route()` call injects a real axis payload; no more silent failures; CLAUDE.md references resolve.

---

### Phase 1 — Schema reform (split weight-quant from KV-quant)

**Goal:** `ModelEntry` can express the two independent quantization axes.

- **Modify** `src/cohezion/inference/registry.py`:
  - Add `WeightQuant` StrEnum: `INT4`, `INT8`, `Q4_K_M`, `Q5_K_M`, `MXFP4`, `BF16`, `FP16`, `QUAROT_INT4`, `API`.
  - Add `KVQuant` dataclass: `scheme: Literal["none","turboquant","quarot","kv8"] = "none"`, `bits: float = 16.0`, `hadamard_size: int = 128`, `qjl_correction: bool = False`, `asymmetric_kv: bool = False` (K=rotated, V=fp16 for dense models per research findings), plus `runtime_flag: dict[str, str] = {}` mapping runtime → CLI flag value (e.g. `{"vllm": "tbq4", "llama.cpp": "turbo3", "sglang": "tbq4"}`) so `fleet.py` emits the right token per backend without caller churn.
  - Replace `ModelEntry.quantization: str` with `weight_quant: WeightQuant` + `kv_quant: KVQuant`.
  - Migrate the 10 existing entries. Examples:
    - Gemma-4-E2B NPU: `weight_quant=WeightQuant.INT4`, `kv_quant=KVQuant(scheme="none", bits=16.0)` — NPU has no TurboQuant operator yet.
    - Gemma-4-E4B iGPU ROCWMMA: `weight_quant=WeightQuant.Q4_K_M`, `kv_quant=KVQuant(scheme="turboquant", bits=3.5, hadamard_size=128, qjl_correction=True, asymmetric_kv=True)`.
    - Gemma-4-26B MoE iGPU Unified: `weight_quant=WeightQuant.MXFP4`, `kv_quant=KVQuant(scheme="turboquant", bits=4.0, hadamard_size=128, qjl_correction=True)`.
    - Gemma-4-31B CPU: `weight_quant=WeightQuant.Q4_K_M`, `kv_quant=KVQuant(scheme="none")` — honest (no AVX kernels).
- **Backward-compat:** deprecated `.quantization` property returns a `"{weight}+{kv.scheme}"` string so any remaining external readers don't break.
- **Tests:** `tests/inference/test_registry.py` extended — every ModelEntry deserializes, `quantization` property produces the legacy string, `kv_quant.bits == 16.0` when scheme is "none".

**Deliverable:** schema expresses reality; no more `"INT4+turboquant"` misnomers.

---

### Phase 2 — Torch ground-truth reference (correctness gate)

**Goal:** Have an oracle to validate every production kernel against. Per CLAUDE.md: "Prove correctness BEFORE measuring performance."

- **Create** `src/cohezion/inference/turboquant_reference.py` (< 300 lines):
  - `HadamardRotation(seed, size)` — reproducible Walsh-Hadamard via `torch.matmul` (accept slow; this is the oracle).
  - `PolarQuant.encode(kv_tensor, bits)` / `.decode(quantized, scale, zero)` — Lloyd-Max scalar quant, Beta-distribution-aware.
  - `QJLResidual(bits=1)` — 1-bit Johnson-Lindenstrauss residual correction.
  - `TurboQuantReference.compress(kv, cfg: KVQuant)` / `.decompress(...)` — single entry point.
- **Dependency:** add `turboquant-torch` to `pyproject.toml` optional `[inference-dev]` extra; gate the reference impl behind `try: import turboquant_torch` so CI without it still passes.
- **Tests:** `tests/inference/test_turboquant_reference.py` with tolerances from the paper:
  - Inner-product distortion b=3 → ≤ 0.03 (paper bound).
  - Round-trip cosine sim ≥ 0.997 at 4-bit, ≥ 0.94 at 2-bit (research expectations).
  - Asymmetric K-rotate / V-pass-through matches vanilla attention logit distribution within 1e-3 relative.
  - Hadamard seed reproducibility (same seed → identical output).

**Deliverable:** a <1 ms/call oracle that production paths must match within published tolerance.

---

### Phase 3 — iGPU production lane (Phase-0b-selected backend)

**Goal:** Real throughput + KV memory gain on the 40 CU iGPU, using whichever
stack Phase 0b's probe validated as stable.

Three vetted backends go in as siblings; one is selected per-lane via
`ModelEntry.llamacpp_backend` (renamed to `runtime_backend` for accuracy):

**Option A — vLLM-rocm (ROCm 7.2.2) — PDF primary recommendation**
- Install under `~/.venvs/cohezion_vllm` (isolated from dev venv).
- Launcher `scripts/launch_vllm_lane.sh` on **port :13308** (iGPU Unified lane):
  ```bash
  source ~/.cohezion/strix_halo.env
  python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "unsloth/Llama-3.5-70B-Q4_K_M" \
    --kv-cache-dtype tbq4 \
    --max-model-len 131072 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
    --enforce-eager --device cuda \
    --port 13308
  ```
- Update registry entry for the iGPU Unified lane: `runtime_backend="vllm_rocm"`, `kv_quant=KVQuant(scheme="turboquant", bits=4.0, runtime_flag={"vllm": "tbq4"})`.

**Option B — Upstream llama.cpp PR #20969 — secondary**
- Build from upstream repo (no third-party fork), checkout PR branch:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp
  git fetch origin pull/20969/head:turboquant-exp && git checkout turboquant-exp
  make GGML_HIP=1 AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1150 -j$(nproc)   # gfx1150 alias works on 1151
  ```
- Launcher binds to **port :13307** (iGPU ROCWMMA lane): `llama-server --kv-cache-type turbo3 -c 131072 --port 13307 -m <gguf>`.
- Keep this option live even if Option A becomes primary — it's a useful sanity check and a fallback path.

**Option C — SGLang PR #21617 — tertiary (high-throughput serving)**
- Scaffolded but not launched by default: `scripts/build_sglang_turboquant.sh` documents the steps (`git fetch origin pull/21617/head:feat-turboquant`, `pip install -e "python[all]"`). Flip on via `COHEZION_SGLANG=1` for multi-user serving experiments.

**Vulkan RADV fallback** (per earlier web research) — if Phase 0b shows ROCm 7.2.2 regresses on gfx1151, stock `llama.cpp` + Vulkan RADV (no TBQ) runs on the same ports; `KVQuant(scheme="none")`. Documented in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` as the escape hatch.

**Fleet wiring (applies to all options):**
- Extend `fleet._dispatch_openai_compatible` (`fleet.py:126-219`) to emit the right flag per `runtime_backend`:
  - vLLM: already set at server launch, no per-request payload field needed; fleet just dispatches normally.
  - llama.cpp: add `extra_body={"kv_cache": {"type": cfg.runtime_flag["llama.cpp"]}}` (ignored by stock; consumed by PR #20969 branch).
  - SGLang: OpenAI-compatible with the TBQ flag accepted at `extra_body["kv_cache_dtype"]`.
- Health probe (`health.py`) learns a `kv_scheme_echo` check per backend: POST a 1-token dummy, parse runtime-specific metadata (`response.headers["x-tbq-scheme"]` for vLLM, usage block for llama.cpp), mark DEGRADED if the declared scheme doesn't match the config.
- Tests: `tests/inference/test_fleet.py` parametrized over `runtime_backend` — verifies the right dispatch variant fires for each backend and never for CPU/cloud.

**Deliverable:** :13307 (llama.cpp PR), :13308 (vLLM-rocm) serve with live TurboQuant KV; a 128k-token prompt fits on 70B where it previously couldn't.

---

### Phase 4 — NPU lane (Ryzen AI 1.7.1 + AMD Quark QuaRot weight rotation)

**Goal:** Best we can do on XDNA 2 without a TurboQuant NPU operator.

- **Pin** Ryzen AI Software to 1.7.1 (hotfix Apr 8, 2026) in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md`.
- **Add** AMD Quark 0.10 to `[inference-dev]` extras (`amd-quark>=0.10`).
- **Create** `scripts/quark_quarot_gemma4_e2b.py` — one-shot offline script that:
  - Loads Gemma-4-E2B weights,
  - Applies Quark's QuaRot rotation (random-rotation flavor, closest to TurboQuant),
  - Exports back to INT4 GGUF for the FLM backend at :13306.
- **Update** the registry entry for Gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF: `weight_quant=WeightQuant.QUAROT_INT4`.
- **Document** in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` that KV-cache TurboQuant on XDNA 2 is **blocked upstream** on AMD compiler support; revisit when Ryzen AI 1.8 drops (est. Q3 2026).
- **Tests:** `tests/inference/test_registry.py` — QuaRot entry roundtrips; `scripts/quark_quarot_gemma4_e2b.py --dry-run` executes without loading weights (import-time check only; real conversion is a one-shot).

**Deliverable:** NPU lane gets a rotation-quantized weight path (the closest family member) while KV stays FP16 until AMD lands the operator.

---

### Phase 5 — Reproducible benchmarks (replace informal numbers)

**Goal:** Replace the 5-call warm observations in `SHOWCASE.md` with statistically valid measurements, populate `ModelEntry.observed_*` fields.

- **Create** `scripts/benchmarks/fleet_ttft.py`:
  - 20 prompts of varied length (256 / 2k / 8k / 32k tokens) × 4 local lanes = 80 dispatches with streaming enabled.
  - Records TTFT p50/p95, tokens/sec, peak RSS, KV memory (via `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/mem_info_vram_used`).
  - Writes JSON to `benchmarks/fleet_report_2026-04-18.json` and a human summary to `benchmarks/fleet_report.md`.
- **KV compression ratio measurement:** 32k-token prompt measured twice — once with Phase 3's TurboQuant-on build, once with a `--no-turboquant` rebuild of the same llama.cpp fork. Report the ratio; target ≥ 4× at 4-bit.
- **Post-benchmark:** update `registry.py` typed latency fields, remove the informal notes paragraph.
- **Add** the 20-prompt harness to `make bench-fleet` (new target in `Makefile`).

**Deliverable:** honest numbers in the registry; a reproducible harness so future regressions are caught.

---

## Files to create / modify

### Create
| Path | Purpose |

| `src/cohezion/core/symmetry_hardware_bridge.py` | Resolves silent `ImportError` in `fleet.py:112` |
| `src/cohezion/inference/turboquant_reference.py` | Torch oracle (< 300 lines) |

| `scripts/probe_backend.py` | Phase 0b bake-off: ROCm 7.2.2 vs Vulkan RADV |
| `scripts/launch_vllm_lane.sh` | Option A: vLLM-rocm on :13308 with `--kv-cache-dtype tbq4` |
| `scripts/build_llamacpp_turboquant.sh` | Option B: upstream llama.cpp PR #20969 build (`GGML_HIP=1`) |
| `scripts/launch_llamacpp_lane.sh` | Option B: llama-server on :13307 with `--kv-cache-type turbo3` |
| `scripts/build_sglang_turboquant.sh` | Option C: SGLang PR #21617 scaffold (not launched by default) |

### Modify

- `health.check_fleet()` (`health.py`) — already lane-aware; add one probe method.
- `ModelEntry.observed_*` fields (`registry.py:75-81`) — already defined as `None`; benchmark harness fills them.

---

## Verification

**After Phase 0:**
```bash
uv run pytest -q tests/inference/test_symmetry_bridge.py
COHEZION_STRICT_AXIS=1 uv run python -c "import asyncio; from cohezion.inference import route; asyncio.run(route('hello', task='routing'))"
# Must succeed — proves bridge is no longer silently absent.
```

**After Phase 1:**
```bash
uv run pytest -q tests/inference/test_registry.py
uv run python -c "from cohezion.inference import get_registry; r = get_registry(); print({m.model_id: (m.weight_quant, m.kv_quant.scheme) for m in r.models.values()})"
```

**After Phase 2:**
```bash
uv run pytest -q tests/inference/test_turboquant_reference.py
# All paper-bound tolerances pass.
```

**After Phase 0b (backend selection):**
```bash
bash scripts/probe_backend.py --prompt-size 32768
# Open benchmarks/backend_probe_2026-04-18.md — confirm the chosen primary.
```

**After Phase 3 (the real end-to-end):**
```bash
source ~/.cohezion/strix_halo.env
# Option A — vLLM-rocm (if Phase 0b selected ROCm 7.2.2 as stable):
bash scripts/launch_vllm_lane.sh &         # :13308 up with --kv-cache-dtype tbq4
# Option B — upstream llama.cpp PR #20969 (always):
bash scripts/build_llamacpp_turboquant.sh  # ~10 min first time
bash scripts/launch_llamacpp_lane.sh &     # :13307 up with --kv-cache-type turbo3

uv run pytest -q tests/inference/           # all green
uv run python scripts/benchmarks/fleet_ttft.py --prompts 4 --lanes igpu_rocwmma,igpu_unified --ctx 32768
# Inspect benchmarks/fleet_report_*.json — confirm kv_cache_scheme = turboquant echoed per backend.
# 128k smoke test against the vLLM lane specifically:
curl -s http://localhost:13308/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"unsloth/Llama-3.5-70B-Q4_K_M","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":32}' | jq .
```

**After Phase 4:**
```bash
uv run python scripts/quark_quarot_gemma4_e2b.py --dry-run  # import-time only
# Real conversion is a manual one-shot and out-of-band for CI.
```

**After Phase 5 (final gate):**
```bash
make bench-fleet       # 80 dispatches, ~15 min wall-clock
uv run pytest -q       # full suite still green (6,100+ tests)
make lint && make type-check
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. `grep -rn 'INT4+turboquant' src/` returns 0 matches (schema reform complete).
2. `fleet._inject_symmetry_axis` injects a real `turboquant_axis` dict — verifiable in logs.
3. :13307 responds with `kv_cache_scheme: "turboquant"` in response metadata for at least one dispatch.
4. `benchmarks/fleet_report.md` shows ≥4× KV-memory reduction on the 32k prompt (TurboQuant on vs off).
5. All typed `observed_ttft_ms_p50/p95` fields in registry.py populated; informal notes removed.
6. Full test suite `uv run pytest -q` green; no new files >300 lines (CLAUDE.md rule).

---

## Out of scope

- Third-party forks (Pascal-SAPUI5/llama.cpp-turboquant, 0xSero/turboquant) — superseded by upstream PRs #20969 (llama.cpp) and #21617 (SGLang), plus vLLM-rocm nightly. Third-party references kept only as citations, not vendored.
- Custom Triton kernel authoring — the Apr 17 PDF sketch (`fused_rotate_quantize_kernel`) is interesting reference material only. We ride SGLang PR #21617's kernels for Option C rather than authoring new ones.
- CPU lane AVX-512 TurboQuant — no public kernels; would be a research project.
- XDNA 2 NPU KV compression — blocked on AMD Ryzen AI compiler operator support (est. Q3 2026 at earliest).
- Cloud-lane changes (Ollama, Claude, Gemini) — TurboQuant is a local inference optimization; cloud lanes untouched.
- BIOS flashing / firmware bisection — Phase 0a is user-gated with explicit confirmation at each destructive step. The agent does not flash BIOS unattended.

---

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm 7.2.2 "stable on gfx1151" claim doesn't hold in practice (source conflict between PDFs and community benchmarks) | Medium | Phase 0b probe is the gate; if it regresses, Phase 3 ships Option B (llama.cpp PR #20969 with HIP) as primary and Option A becomes documented-future. |
| Upstream llama.cpp PR #20969 rebases or is closed before integration | Medium | Pin the specific SHA from `git fetch origin pull/20969/head` at the point we build; archive the diff in `vendor/notes.md`; cherry-pick-able if the PR rebases. |
| Kernel 6.18.4 from ppa:cappelikan breaks other drivers on the Framework | Low | Phase 0a is user-gated; user keeps previous kernel as GRUB default; BIOS not touched until probe succeeds. |
| Paper-tolerance tests flake due to random seed drift | Low | Reference impl exposes `seed` param; tests pin seed explicitly; use `torch.manual_seed` fixtures. |
| AMD Quark QuaRot rotation degrades Gemma-4-E2B quality | Medium | Run needle-in-haystack eval before/after; keep un-rotated GGUF as rollback at :13306. |
| `extra_body.kv_cache` field causes stock llama.cpp to 400-error | Low | Stock llama.cpp ignores unknown fields (verified in research). Add a feature-flag bypass for safety. |
| Benchmark harness overruns the 32 GB swap on 32k-prompt 70B runs | Low | Harness checks `/proc/meminfo` before each lane; skips if available < 8 GB. |
| Drift risk: user might want "one more thing" after 3 failed tuning attempts (CLAUDE.md strategy pivot) | Medium | Phase 5 benchmark is the pivot trigger. If TurboQuant yields <1.5× KV reduction in practice, STOP and reassess rather than parameter-tune. |

---

## Effort estimate

| Phase | Engineer-hours |
|---|---|
| Phase 0a (kernel/firmware/BIOS) | 1-2 (user-gated reboots) |
| Phase 0b (ROCm vs Vulkan probe) | 2-3 |
| Phase 0 (silent-failure unblock) | 2-3 |
| Phase 1 (schema reform) | 3-4 |
| Phase 2 (torch oracle) | 4-6 (paper-tolerance tests are the long pole) |
| Phase 3 (three-backend production) | 10-14 (vLLM + llama.cpp PR + SGLang scaffold) |
| Phase 4 (NPU + Quark QuaRot) | 3-4 |
| Phase 5 (benchmarks) | 4-6 (benchmark runs are wall-clock bound) |
| **Total** | **29-42 engineer-hours** |

Matches the research's "2-4 week engineering effort" band but compressed by
layering torch oracle + production fork so we avoid re-deriving paper internals.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Probe Strix Halo BIOS + host state without requiring sudo.

Reports what the OS exposes and flags what must be verified manually in the
Framework Desktop BIOS. Invoke before Phase 0a of the TurboQuant plan
(.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md) to know which settings are already
right and which still need a physical BIOS visit.

Usage:
    uv run python scripts/check_bios_state.py

No sudo, no writes, no network. Safe to run any time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import glob
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

# Targets from HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md (April 18, 2026 baseline).
TARGET_KERNEL_MAJOR_MINOR_PATCH: tuple[int, int, int] = (6, 18, 4)
TARGET_VRAM_GB_MIN = 100  # Auto UMA on kernel 6.18.4 should report ≥ ~108 GB.
TARGET_PCIE_SPEED_GTS = 32.0  # Gen5 = 32 GT/s.
TARGET_GPU_TARGET = "gfx1151"


def _run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return ""
    return out.stdout


def check_kernel() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    release = _run(["uname", "-r"]).strip()
    m = re.match(r"(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", release)
    if not m:
        return False, f"unable to parse uname -r: {release!r}"
    version = tuple(int(x) for x in m.groups())
    ok = version >= TARGET_KERNEL_MAJOR_MINOR_PATCH
    verdict = "OK" if ok else f"BELOW TARGET ({'.'.join(map(str, TARGET_KERNEL_MAJOR_MINOR_PATCH))}+)"
    return ok, f"{release} — {verdict}"


def check_gpu_target() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if shutil.which("rocminfo") is None:
        return False, "rocminfo not on PATH — ROCm not installed?"
    out = _run(["rocminfo"])
    if TARGET_GPU_TARGET in out:
        return True, f"{TARGET_GPU_TARGET} detected via rocminfo"
    return False, f"{TARGET_GPU_TARGET} NOT found in rocminfo output"


def check_vram_allocation() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Read VRAM total from sysfs — reflects current BIOS UMA setting."""
    candidates = sorted(glob.glob("/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total"))
    if not candidates:
        return False, "no /sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total found"
    for path in candidates:
        try:
            total_bytes = int(Path(path).read_text().strip())
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            continue
        total_gb = total_bytes / (1024**3)
        device = Path(path).parent.name
        ok = total_gb >= TARGET_VRAM_GB_MIN
        verdict = "OK (Auto UMA likely)" if ok else "LOW — BIOS UMA likely set to a fixed small value"
        return ok, f"{device}: {total_gb:.1f} GB — {verdict}"
    return False, "all VRAM sysfs reads failed"


def check_pcie_speed() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Parse lspci output for GPU link speed. Works without sudo, less detail."""
    if shutil.which("lspci") is None:
        return False, "lspci not available"
    # Find AMD VGA/display controllers first.
    vga_lines = [ln for ln in _run(["lspci"]).splitlines() if "VGA" in ln or "Display" in ln]
    amd_devs = [ln.split()[0] for ln in vga_lines if "AMD" in ln or "ATI" in ln]
    if not amd_devs:
        return False, "no AMD VGA/Display device found via lspci"

    # lspci -vv requires root for full detail on many systems; fall back gracefully.
    for dev in amd_devs:
        detail = _run(["lspci", "-vv", "-s", dev])
        m = re.search(r"LnkSta:\s+Speed\s+([\d.]+)GT/s", detail)
        if m:
            speed = float(m.group(1))
            ok = speed >= TARGET_PCIE_SPEED_GTS
            verdict = "OK (Gen5)" if ok else f"BELOW Gen5 (Gen{int(speed/8)}?)"
            return ok, f"{dev}: {speed} GT/s — {verdict}"
    return False, "lspci -vv did not expose LnkSta (may need sudo for this device)"


def check_cpu_features() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Check AMD Zen 5 CPU flags relevant to CPU-lane inference.

    AMX is Intel-only (Sapphire Rapids+); AMD Zen 5 has AVX-512 with VNNI
    and BF16 sub-extensions instead. CLAUDE.md's 'AVX-512 + VNNI + AMX'
    line predates verification and is wrong for this silicon.
    """
    out = _run(["lscpu"])
    flags = ""
    for ln in out.splitlines():
        if ln.lower().startswith("flags:"):
            flags = ln.lower()
            break
    wanted = {"avx512f", "avx512_vnni", "avx512_bf16"}
    present = {w for w in wanted if w in flags}
    ok = present == wanted
    verdict = "OK" if ok else f"missing {sorted(wanted - present)}"
    return ok, f"AVX-512 / VNNI / BF16 — {verdict}"


def check_rocm_version() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if shutil.which("rocminfo") is None:
        return False, "ROCm not installed (rocminfo missing)"
    ver_path = Path("/opt/rocm/.info/version")
    if ver_path.exists():
        return True, f"/opt/rocm/.info/version = {ver_path.read_text().strip()}"
    return True, "ROCm present but version file not found (check `/opt/rocm/.info/`)"


def check_user_groups() -> tuple[bool, str]:
    out = _run(["id", "-Gn"]).strip().split()
    needed = {"render", "video"}
    have = needed & set(out)
    ok = have == needed
    missing = needed - have
    verdict = "OK" if ok else f"MISSING {sorted(missing)} (run: sudo usermod -aG {','.join(sorted(missing))} $USER; log out/in)"
    return ok, f"groups: {' '.join(sorted(have)) or 'none'} — {verdict}"


def main() -> int:
    checks = [
        ("Kernel", check_kernel),
        ("GPU target (gfx1151)", check_gpu_target),
        ("VRAM allocation (UMA)", check_vram_allocation),
        ("PCIe link speed", check_pcie_speed),
        ("CPU features", check_cpu_features),
        ("ROCm version", check_rocm_version),
        ("User groups", check_user_groups),
    ]
    print("=" * 72)
    print("Strix Halo state probe — .claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md")
    print("=" * 72)
    all_ok = True
    for name, fn in checks:
        ok, detail = fn()
        mark = "✓" if ok else "✗"
        print(f"  [{mark}] {name:<28} {detail}")
        all_ok = all_ok and ok

    print()
    print("Things this probe CANNOT check (verify manually in BIOS):")
    print("  - AI Max Performance Mode = Enabled  (no OS-side API)")
    print("  - UMA Frame Buffer = Auto            (VRAM row above is a proxy,")
    print("                                        but can't distinguish 'Auto'")
    print("                                        from 'fixed 96 GB')")
    print()
    if all_ok:
        print("Verdict: baseline looks good. BIOS visit MAY still be needed to")
        print("confirm AI Max Performance Mode is Enabled.")
        return 0
    print("Verdict: at least one item below target. BIOS visit and/or")
    print("kernel/firmware/ROCm work required — see plan Phase 0a.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## Python Development Standards

**Standards:** Always use uv | pytest for tests | ruff for quality | Self-documenting code

### Package Management — UV ONLY

`uv pip install`, `uv run python`, `uv run pytest`. **Never bare `pip`.**

### Testing & Quality — MINIMIZE OUTPUT

```bash
uv run pytest -q                                    # Quiet mode (ALWAYS)
uv run pytest -q --cov=src --cov-fail-under=80     # Coverage
ruff format . && ruff check . --fix                 # Format + lint
basedpyright src                                    # Type check
```

**Never use `-v`/`-s` unless debugging a specific test.** Verbose output burns context.

For many errors, fix incrementally — don't dump 100+ errors into context.

### Code Style

- **Type hints:** Required on public functions. Modern syntax: `list[int]`, `str | None`
- **Docstrings:** One-line for most. Multi-line only for complex logic. Skip if name is self-explanatory.
- **Imports:** stdlib → third-party → local. `ruff check . --fix` auto-sorts.
- **No bare `except`.** Catch specific exceptions.
- **Use `pathlib`** over `os.path`. Use context managers for resources.

### Project Config

Python 3.12+. Dependencies in `pyproject.toml`. Tests use `@pytest.mark.unit`/`@pytest.mark.integration`.

### Verification

`uv run pytest -q` → `ruff format .` → `ruff check .` → `basedpyright src` → coverage >= 80% → no file > 300 lines.

### ⚡ Measurement Integrity
- **Report actual numbers**: 2,675/2,700 passing (98.1%) > 1,599 passing (inflated)
- **Flag discrepancies**: If independent test shows different count, request re-verification immediately
- **Verify claims**: "Complete" = files exist AND tests pass, not projected

### ⚡ Surgical Commits Against High-Churn Trees (Learning 363)
When the working tree has unrelated churn (BMAD upgrades, pre-existing untracked, other sprints) and you need a clean commit:
- Enumerate paths explicitly in a handoff markdown before staging — no wildcards, no `git add .`
- Verify the staged set with `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -iE "<churn-pattern>"` returning empty before committing
- Prefer two focused commits (feature + follow-ups) over a single squash when the narratives are distinct — cherry-picking to a fresh branch off `main` preserves the separation without dragging unrelated history

### ⚡ V-Model Structural-Before-Behavioral (Learning 366)
Every behavioral invariant whose failure surface is a keyword/signature drift should have a paired *structural* invariant at the harness layer:
- Behavioral test would fail with `TypeError: got unexpected keyword argument` deep in the call stack — hard to diagnose
- Structural check (`inspect.signature(fn).parameters.get(name)`) fires at harness start with an explicit invariant name (e.g. "O3b: fn.run accepts budget_usd kwarg")
- Structural check cost: ~1ms; pays for itself the first time a refactor drifts a signature

### ⚡ Diagnostic Sidecars (Learning 362)
When a summary table truncates diagnostic data AND the failing path is a subprocess that can fail silently, write full stdout+stderr to a sidecar file next to the report. V-Model invariant asserts the sidecar exists when the subprocess had 0 successes. Summary tables are for humans scanning; sidecars are for humans diagnosing.

### ⚡ Adversarial Review in Parallel (INSIGHTS #7)
Spawn 3 concurrent reviewer agents (scientific rigor / edge-case hunting / security) via `Agent` tool in a single message for non-trivial deliverables. Synthesize in main context. Sequential review costs 3× wall-clock and loses cross-pollination; parallel produces a combined review in ~90s + synthesis time. Applied to sprint `sorted-churning-toucan` → 20+ findings, 14 actionable (6 in-session fixes + 3 P0 + 5 P1/P2).

### ⚡ Additive Composition Under Directive Changes (INSIGHTS #11)
When the user redirects mid-sprint (e.g. "now do X instead of Y"), prefer adding a new module over modifying existing tested code. `cohezion.inference` absorbed 4 mid-sprint pivots (TurboQuant → CLI → GAIA → tiered) by growing from 3 to 7 modules without breaking the original 29 tests. Rule: if a new directive would force editing a passing-test surface, first ask "can this be a new module that composes with the existing one?" Compositional additions don't regress behavior; modifications risk it.

### ⚡ Tiered > Flat Routing (INSIGHTS #2)
`route()` is a dispatch primitive; `TieredOrchestrator` is the composition primitive. Flat routing picks one lane; tiered runs cheap-first, escalates only when quality gates fail. Same 4-lane fleet under orchestration delivers quality-bounded cost curves that flat routing can't express. For any "pick the best provider" problem, ask: is this really one-shot, or should cheaper options be tried first and escalated?

```

```

**User constraints for the remainder of Phase 0a:**
1. The BIOS firmware update path (to unlock Auto-UMA + missing toggles) is

2. **No more reboots unless strictly required by a kernel change.** This rules

3. The ROCm 7.2.1 → 7.2.2 userspace upgrade is still on the table **only if**
   it can be performed without pulling in `amdgpu-dkms` (which would itself
   require reboot).

**Intended outcome.** Freeze Phase 0a on the achievable 64 GB / kernel-6.17 /
ROCm-7.2.1 baseline, document that baseline honestly in
`HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` (Learning 4: "Report honest metrics"), and pivot

`llama.cpp` + Vulkan RADV (without TBQ) is the pragmatic primary backend. The
rest of the parent plan (Phases 0, 1, 2 already committed; Phases 3, 4, 5
remaining) is unchanged in intent; only the Phase 0a baseline assumptions and
the Phase 3 backend-selection criteria need updating.

Llama-3.1-70B Q4\_K\_M at 128k context with 6× KV compression — needs roughly
**42 GB weights + 5 GB compressed KV + 3–5 GB activations ≈ 50–52 GB**. That
fits inside 64 GB with ~12 GB of VRAM headroom for cache-miss spikes and
ROCm's own overhead. The 108 GB target was a ceiling that would have enabled

**Parent plan:** `/home/mike-anderson/.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md`

TurboQuant on the Strix Halo host** — the parent plan's end state. The BIOS

UMA option, no AI Max Performance toggle, and no PCIe Gen5 toggle** (those
appear only on Framework BIOS v3.05+, which the user opted not to flash this
session). The user explicitly stated: *"If we need the kernel upgrade for
TurboQuant then let's do it. I'll just need another email. The goal has been
unlocking TurboQuant."* That reverses the earlier "no reboots" constraint
and puts the kernel / firmware / ROCm upgrades back on the critical path,
with the affordance that each reboot-gated step gets an email-formatted
`*_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` handoff so the user can pick up from anywhere.

**Fresh probe (2026-04-18, post-BIOS):**
```
[✗] Kernel                       6.17.0-1017-oem — BELOW TARGET (6.18.4+)
[✓] GPU target (gfx1151)         gfx1151 detected via rocminfo
[✗] VRAM allocation (UMA)        device: 64.0 GB — LOW
[✗] PCIe link speed              lspci -vv did not expose LnkSta (needs sudo)
[✓] CPU features                 AVX-512 / VNNI / BF16 — OK
[✓] ROCm version                 /opt/rocm/.info/version = 7.2.1
[✓] User groups                  groups: render video — OK
```

**Three reasons the kernel upgrade matters for TurboQuant specifically:**
1. **Potential VRAM unlock beyond BIOS cap.** The parent plan's research
   (`dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:44`) cites the PDF claim that **kernel 6.18.4
   enables dynamic UMA scaling beyond the BIOS fixed cap** ("UMA dynamically
   scales to ~112 GB on 6.18.4 (up from 96 GB BIOS cap)"). If that holds, the
   kernel upgrade could lift the 64 GB ceiling without a BIOS firmware
   update — the kernel treats the BIOS value as a reservation, then grows
   into the unified 128 GB LPDDR5X pool on demand. This is the single
   highest-leverage gain we can make in Phase 0a.
2. **`HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.0` expected behavior.** The parent plan's
   env-pin (`dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:88-96`) assumes a kernel that cleanly
   reports gfx1151 as 11.5.0; 6.18's AMDGPU has better gfx1151 runtime
   metadata than 6.17's `-oem` backport.
3. **Fixes pre-7.2.x ROCm's >64 GB load bug on gfx1151** (community
   benchmarks; `dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:42-43`). Since we *need* to load a
   70B Q4\_K\_M model (~42 GB) plus KV cache, we want the kernel + ROCm pair
   that the community has verified past the 64 GB load threshold, not the
   one known to regress there.

**Intended outcome.** Bring the host to the parent plan's "April 2026
baseline" via four sudo-gated, reboot-tolerant steps (kernel → firmware →
ROCm → verify), then run the **Phase 0b ROCm vs Vulkan bake-off probe** to
empirically select the primary TurboQuant backend. Each reboot-gated step
produces an email-formatted handoff markdown so the user can pick up after
physically rebooting and re-authenticating.

---

## Recommended approach

A four-step sudo-gated sequence, each with its own email-style handoff, then
the Phase 0b probe. The user pastes the re-probe output into the next Claude
session after each reboot; the agent advances.

### Step 1 — Kernel 6.17 → 6.18.4 (reboot, produces VRAM verdict)

Use `mainline` CLI (not the GUI) from the `ppa:cappelikan/ppa` repository so
the step is automatable and auditable.

```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:cappelikan/ppa -y
sudo apt update
sudo apt install mainline -y
mainline list | grep -E '6\.18\.[0-9]+' | head -5        # confirm 6.18.4 available
sudo mainline install 6.18.4                              # installs to /boot
sudo update-grub                                          # ensure new kernel is default
```

**Handoff artifact:** write `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/KERNEL_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md`
with (a) the reboot instruction, (b) the exact command to re-run the probe,
(c) the resume prompt for the next Claude session.

**Post-reboot verification (user runs, pastes output):**
```bash
cd ~/dev/cohezion/.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker
uname -r                                                  # expect 6.18.4+
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py             # expect kernel row ✓
cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/mem_info_vram_total       # VRAM in bytes — is it > 64 GB?
```

**Decision gate on VRAM row after reboot:**
- If VRAM > 64 GB: the kernel's dynamic UMA scaling engaged. We're past the
  BIOS cap. Record the actual value in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md`.
- If VRAM still = 64 GB: the kernel upgrade helps driver stability but not
  capacity. 64 GB remains the working ceiling; adjust Phase 3 launch flags
  to `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.72` instead of 0.92.

### Step 2 — AMDGPU `strix_halo*` firmware refresh (reboot)

Only the `strix_halo*` blobs change; no other firmware is touched.

```bash
cd /tmp
git clone --depth 1 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git
cd linux-firmware/amdgpu
ls strix_halo* 2>/dev/null || { echo 'no strix_halo blobs'; exit 1; }
sudo cp strix_halo* /lib/firmware/amdgpu/
sudo update-initramfs -u -k 6.18.4                        # bake new firmware into initramfs
```

**Handoff artifact:** `FIRMWARE_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` (email-formatted,
same shape as `BIOS_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md`).

**Post-reboot verification:**
```bash
dmesg | grep -i 'strix_halo'                              # expect 'loaded' lines
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py             # no regression
```

### Step 3 — ROCm 7.2.1 → 7.2.2 (reboot if DKMS rebuilds)

Now that reboots are acceptable, drop the `apt-mark hold` dance. Let apt
pull in whatever kernel driver the 7.2.2 packages require.

```bash
if ! grep -q 'rocm/apt/7.2.2' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list 2>/dev/null; then
  sudo wget -qO - https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/rocm.gpg.key \
    | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/rocm.gpg
  echo 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/rocm.gpg] https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/apt/7.2.2 noble main' \
    | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/rocm-7.2.2.list
  sudo apt update
fi
sudo apt upgrade -y rocm-hip-sdk rocm-hip-libraries rocminfo rocm-smi-lib
sudo apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'dkms|amdgpu' \
  && echo 'DKMS rebuild pending — reboot required'
```

**Handoff artifact:** `ROCM_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` — only written if the
apt output indicates a DKMS rebuild; otherwise we proceed without reboot.

**Post-upgrade verification:**
```bash
cat /opt/rocm/.info/version                               # expect 7.2.2
rocminfo | grep -E '(gfx1151|Name)'                       # still detects GPU
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py             # all green except maybe PCIe (sudo-gated)
```

### Step 4 — Update `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` with post-upgrade truth

Once all three upgrades are in and the probe is all-green (modulo the
sudo-gated PCIe row, which we'll leave as "unknown without sudo"):

- Record the **actual** post-upgrade numbers (kernel, VRAM, ROCm version).
- Note whether the kernel's dynamic UMA scaling lifted the VRAM ceiling or
  whether 64 GB remained the working cap.
- Mark the BIOS firmware update as "deferred — current BIOS rev. lacks Auto
  UMA / AI Max Perf / PCIe Gen5 toggles; revisit if host sustained perf
  falls short of target in Phase 5 benchmarks."
- Point to this plan file and the three RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md artifacts.

### Step 5 — Phase 0b: run the backend bake-off probe (the real TurboQuant unlock)

This is the parent plan's Phase 0b (lines 110–129 of
`dreamy-jingling-thacker.md`) executed against the post-upgrade baseline.

```bash
uv venv ~/.venvs/tbq_probe
. ~/.venvs/tbq_probe/bin/activate
uv pip install --pre vllm-rocm \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/rocm7.2
# Ensure stock llama.cpp + Vulkan RADV is available for the control arm
which llama-server || sudo apt install -y llama-cpp-tools    # or build from source
```

Then create `scripts/probe_backend.py` (< 120 lines per parent-plan budget)
that runs two timed 32k-token dispatches:
1. **Arm A — vLLM-rocm + TurboQuant:** `vllm serve
   unsloth/Llama-3.1-70B-Q4_K_M --kv-cache-dtype tbq4 --max-model-len 131072
   --gpu-memory-utilization <0.72 if VRAM capped at 64GB, else 0.92>
   --enforce-eager --device cuda --port 13308`, then a 32k-token prompt via
   the OpenAI-compatible client.
2. **Arm B — Vulkan RADV control:** same GGUF, stock `llama.cpp` +
   `--n-gpu-layers 999`, no TBQ.

Measure for each arm: peak VRAM used
(`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/mem_info_vram_used`), TTFT, tokens/sec,
crash/OOM status, max stable context length. Write
`benchmarks/backend_probe_2026-04-18.md` with the outcome and a **primary
backend recommendation** with exact flags.

**This is the gate the parent plan calls "the evidence-grounded choice" —
Phase 3 cannot start until this recommendation is written.**

### Step 6 — Update the parent plan's Phase 3 assumptions to match the probe

Markdown-only edit to `dreamy-jingling-thacker.md`:
- Set `--gpu-memory-utilization` to the value that fit the probe.
- Promote the winning backend (`vllm_rocm` or `llamacpp_vulkan`) to primary
  in Phase 3's Option A vs Option B ordering.
- Update the Phase 0a verification gate (line 98-104) to reflect the
  actual-achievable VRAM number (may be 64 GB, may be higher if dynamic UMA
  engaged).

---

### Create
| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/KERNEL_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` | Email-style handoff for Step 1 reboot |
| `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/FIRMWARE_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` | Email-style handoff for Step 2 reboot |
| `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/ROCM_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` | Conditional — only if ROCm upgrade triggers a DKMS reboot |
| `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/scripts/probe_backend.py` | Phase 0b two-arm bake-off; < 120 lines |
| `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/benchmarks/backend_probe_2026-04-18.md` | Probe outcome + primary backend recommendation |

### Modify
| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` (worktree) | Post-upgrade kernel/VRAM/ROCm values; BIOS limitations; pointer to this plan |
| `/home/mike-anderson/.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md` | Phase 0a verification gate numbers; Phase 3 `--gpu-memory-utilization`; primary-backend ordering |

### Reuse (do not reinvent)
- `scripts/check_bios_state.py` — the read-only probe; re-run after each reboot.
- `BIOS_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` — template shape for the three new email-style handoffs; keep voice and structure consistent.
- `fleet._dispatch_openai_compatible` (`fleet.py:126-219`) — OpenAI-compatible dispatch pattern for Arm A of the probe.
- `cohezion.inference.registry.ModelEntry.observed_*` — populated later in parent plan's Phase 5; Phase 0b writes only to the probe markdown.

---

## Verification

**After Step 1 (kernel upgrade + reboot):**
```bash
uname -r                                                   # 6.18.4 or later
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py              # kernel row ✓
cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/mem_info_vram_total        # is it > 64 GB now?
```

**After Step 2 (firmware refresh + reboot):**

```bash

```

**After Step 4 (hardware profile amended):**
```bash

```

```bash

```

**After Step 6 (parent plan amended):**
```bash
grep 'gpu-memory-utilization' /home/mike-anderson/.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md
# matches the probe's winning value (0.72 if 64 GB ceiling held, 0.92 if dynamic UMA unlocked it)
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. `uname -r` reports 6.18.4+ and the probe's kernel row is ✓.
2. `strix_halo*` firmware blobs are loaded per dmesg.
3. ROCm version reads 7.2.2 from `/opt/rocm/.info/version`.
4. `benchmarks/backend_probe_2026-04-18.md` names a primary backend and lists the exact CLI flags that served a 32k-token prompt without OOM/crash.
5. `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` reflects the actual post-upgrade numbers, not the target numbers.
6. Each reboot was preceded by an `*_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` email-style handoff so the user could pick up in a new Claude session.

---

## Out of scope (this plan)

- **Framework BIOS firmware update.** Current BIOS lacks Auto-UMA / AI Max
  Performance / PCIe Gen5 toggles; user-gated decision, deferred. Revisit
  only if Phase 5 benchmarks show the missing toggles are the bottleneck.
- **Parent plan's Phases 3, 4, 5.** Start *after* Step 5 produces a primary
  backend. This plan stops at the Phase 0b exit so the parent plan can
  resume cleanly with evidence-grounded defaults.
- **Custom Triton kernel authoring.** Parent plan's Phase 3 rides upstream
  PRs; this plan does not change that posture.

---

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Mainline 6.18.4 kernel hangs on boot / breaks Wi-Fi or other drivers on the Framework Desktop | Low | GRUB retains the 6.17.0-1017-oem entry; user can select it at boot. `KERNEL_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` includes the rollback step (`sudo mainline uninstall 6.18.4` from rescue). |
| Kernel 6.18.4 does *not* lift the VRAM cap above 64 GB (PDF's "dynamic UMA scaling" claim doesn't hold on this BIOS) | Medium | Parent plan's Phase 3 already has the `0.72` fallback flag; Step 1's post-reboot gate branches cleanly on the VRAM reading. |
| AMDGPU `strix_halo*` firmware blob refresh introduces a regression visible only under load | Low | `/lib/firmware/amdgpu/` is backed up in `/lib/firmware/amdgpu.bak/` before the `cp`; rollback is one `cp -r` + reboot. |
| ROCm 7.2.2 breaks something ROCm 7.2.1 had working (e.g., pytorch-rocm wheels) | Low-Medium | Phase 0b's control arm (Vulkan RADV) is driver-independent, so we always have at least one working inference path; also, ROCm 7.2.1 `.deb` files remain cached in `/var/cache/apt/archives/` for fast revert. |
| vLLM-rocm nightly OOMs loading 42 GB weights into 64 GB VRAM even at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.72` | Medium | Phase 0b detects this; Vulkan RADV becomes primary; TurboQuant is documented as "blocked on this host until BIOS firmware update unlocks Auto UMA". |
| Three reboots stretch across multiple Claude sessions and the user loses thread | Low | Each reboot has its own `*_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` with the exact resume prompt; parent plan's commit log anchors progress. |
| `scripts/probe_backend.py` creeps past 120 lines | Low | Keep the two arms as separate functions; no framework, no class hierarchy. |

---

## Effort estimate

| Step | Wall-clock |
|---|---|
| Step 1 — Kernel 6.17 → 6.18.4 + reboot + re-probe | 20–30 min (apt + mainline install + reboot + verification) |
| Step 2 — Firmware refresh + reboot + re-probe | 15–20 min |
| Step 3 — ROCm 7.2.2 upgrade (± reboot) | 15–25 min |
| Step 4 — Amend `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md` | 5 min |
| Step 5 — Phase 0b probe (venv + install + two 32k runs) | 25–40 min |
| Step 6 — Update parent plan | 5 min |
| **Total** | **~90–125 min, 2–3 reboots, 3 email handoffs** |

# Phase 0a Completion: Kernel + Firmware + ROCm → Phase 0b Probe (the TurboQuant Unlock)

**Plan created:** 2026-04-18
**Parent plan:** `/home/mike-anderson/.claude/plans/dreamy-jingling-thacker.md`
**Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker`
**Branch:** `spec/dreamy-jingling-thacker`

---

## Context

**Why this plan exists.** The goal is and has always been **unlocking
TurboQuant on the Strix Halo host** — the parent plan's end state. The BIOS
step has partially completed: VRAM moved from 0.5 GB → 64 GB after the user's
BIOS visit, but the user's current Framework BIOS revision **has no "Auto"
UMA option, no AI Max Performance toggle, and no PCIe Gen5 toggle** (those
appear only on Framework BIOS v3.05+, which the user opted not to flash this
session). The user explicitly stated: *"If we need the kernel upgrade for
TurboQuant then let's do it. I'll just need another email. The goal has been
unlocking TurboQuant."* That reverses the earlier "no reboots" constraint
and puts the kernel / firmware / ROCm upgrades back on the critical path,
with the affordance that each reboot-gated step gets an email-formatted
`*_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` handoff so the user can pick up from anywhere.

**Fresh probe (2026-04-18, post-BIOS):**
```
[✗] Kernel                       6.17.0-1017-oem — BELOW TARGET (6.18.4+)
[✓] GPU target (gfx1151)         gfx1151 detected via rocminfo
[✗] VRAM allocation (UMA)        device: 64.0 GB — LOW
[✗] PCIe link speed              lspci -vv did not expose LnkSta (needs sudo)
[✓] CPU features                 AVX-512 / VNNI / BF16 — OK
[✓] ROCm version                 /opt/rocm/.info/version = 7.2.1
[✓] User groups                  groups: render video — OK
```

**Three reasons the kernel upgrade matters for TurboQuant specifically:**
1. **Potential VRAM unlock beyond BIOS cap.** The parent plan's research
   (`dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:44`) cites the PDF claim that **kernel 6.18.4
   enables dynamic UMA scaling beyond the BIOS fixed cap** ("UMA dynamically
   scales to ~112 GB on 6.18.4 (up from 96 GB BIOS cap)"). If that holds, the
   kernel upgrade could lift the 64 GB ceiling without a BIOS firmware
   update — the kernel treats the BIOS value as a reservation, then grows
   into the unified 128 GB LPDDR5X pool on demand. This is the single
   highest-leverage gain we can make in Phase 0a.
2. **`HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.0` expected behavior.** The parent plan's
   env-pin (`dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:88-96`) assumes a kernel that cleanly
   reports gfx1151 as 11.5.0; 6.18's AMDGPU has better gfx1151 runtime
   metadata than 6.17's `-oem` backport.
3. **Fixes pre-7.2.x ROCm's >64 GB load bug on gfx1151** (community
   benchmarks; `dreamy-jingling-thacker.md:42-43`). Since we *need* to load a
   70B Q4\_K\_M model (~42 GB) plus KV cache, we want the kernel + ROCm pair
   that the community has verified past the 64 GB load threshold, not the
   one known to regress there.

**Intended outcome.** Bring the host to the parent plan's "April 2026
baseline" via four sudo-gated, reboot-tolerant steps (kernel → firmware →
ROCm → verify), then run the **Phase 0b ROCm vs Vulkan bake-off probe** to
empirically select the primary TurboQuant backend. Each reboot-gated step
produces an email-formatted handoff markdown so the user can pick up after
physically rebooting and re-authenticating.

---

## Recommended approach

A four-step sudo-gated sequence, each with its own email-style handoff, then
the Phase 0b probe. The user pastes the re-probe output into the next Claude
session after each reboot; the agent advances.

### Step 1 — Kernel 6.17 → 6.18.4 (reboot, produces VRAM verdict)

Use `mainline` CLI (not the GUI) from the `ppa:cappelikan/ppa` repository so
the step is automatable and auditable.

```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:cappelikan/ppa -y
sudo apt update
sudo apt install mainline -y
mainline list | grep -E '6\.18\.[0-9]+' | head -5        # confirm 6.18.4 available
sudo mainline install 6.18.4                              # installs to /boot
sudo update-grub                                          # ensure new kernel is default
```

**Handoff artifact:** write `.claude/worktrees/dreamy-jingling-thacker/KERNEL_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md`

```bash

.venv/bin/python scripts/check_bios_state.py             # expect kernel row ✓
cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/mem_info_vram_total       # VRAM in bytes — is it > 64 GB?
```

**Decision gate on VRAM row after reboot:**
- If VRAM > 64 GB: the kernel's dynamic UMA scaling engaged. We're past the

```bash
cd /tmp
git clone --depth 1 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git
cd linux-firmware/amdgpu
ls strix_halo* 2>/dev/null || { echo 'no strix_halo blobs'; exit 1; }
```

| `scripts/probe_backend.py` creeps past 120 lines | Low | Keep the two arms as separate functions; no framework, no class hierarchy. |

"""Send the application summary email to manderson240@gmail.com.

Usage:
    # Set your Gmail App Password first (NOT your regular password):
    # 1. Go to https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords
    # 2. Generate an app password for "Mail"
    # 3. Run:

    python scripts/send_summary_email.py
"""

import os
import smtplib
import ssl
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    password = os.environ.get("GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD")
    if not password:
        print("ERROR: Set GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD environment variable first.")
        print()
        print("Steps:")
        print("  1. Go to https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords")
        print("  2. Generate an app password for 'Mail'")
        print("  3. export GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD='xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx'")
        print("  4. python scripts/send_summary_email.py")
        return

    sender = "manderson240@gmail.com"
    recipient = "manderson240@gmail.com"

    msg = MIMEMultipart("alternative")
    msg["Subject"] = "Cohezion — Anthropic Application Package Ready"
    msg["From"] = sender
    msg["To"] = recipient

import asyncio from cohezion.mcp.email_notifier import EmailNotifier async def main(): notifier = EmailNotifier() subject = "📱 Cohezion Remote Command Guide" body = """

How to Control your Swarm via Phone

You can now send commands to the Cohezion swarm by replying to any alert or sending a new email with the subject starting with [CMD].

Available Commands

  • [CMD] status: Returns active Python/Ollama processes and SurrealDB health.
  • [CMD] report: Sends the latest autonomous research report.
  • [CMD] ping: Simple health check (returns PONG).
  • [CMD] run [script_name]: Starts a script in the scripts/ directory (e.g., [CMD] run mining_sprint).
  • [CMD] resume: Clears resource throttles and signals agents to re-evaluate trajectories.

Proactive Alerts

The swarm will automatically email you if:

  • An agent is Blocked on user input.
  • A Security Block (PromptGuard) is triggered.
  • Resource Limits are hit (GPU/Memory exhaustion).

- Your Cohezion Swarm

""" if notifier.is_available: await notifier.send_email(subject, body, is_html=True) print("Instruction email sent.") if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

A **Step 0 email-delivery test** followed by four sudo-gated upgrades, each
with an actual email handoff (not just a file), then the Phase 0b probe. The
user pastes the re-probe output into the next Claude session after each
reboot; the agent advances.

### Step 0 — Prove email delivery works before depending on it

**Problem state as of this session:** (verified)
- `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` is UNSET in the running shell.
- `EmailNotifier` is imported by 5+ scripts but has no class definition in
  tracked code — an orphaned import; those scripts silently no-op.
- Only working email send in the codebase is the direct
  `smtplib.SMTP_SSL("smtp.gmail.com", 465)` pattern in
  `scripts/send_summary_email.py`, which requires `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` set.
- Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) is installed, so the credential can be pulled lazily
  from the vault rather than pasted into a shell or `.env`.

**Step 0 tasks:**
1. **Retrieve the Gmail App Password.** Preference order: (a) if Bitwarden
   vault has an item named `Gmail App Password` or similar, pull it with
   `bw get password <id>` (user unlocks the vault once with `bw unlock`); (b)
   otherwise, the user generates a new App Password at
   `https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords` and exports it in the
   session with the `!` prefix so it never lands in a file:
   `!export GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD='xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx'`.
2. **Write `scripts/send_handoff.py`** — a single consolidated script (< 80
   lines) that takes `--subject`, `--body-file` (path to a markdown file),
   optional `--to` (defaults to `manderson240@gmail.com`), renders plain
   text + HTML parts (convert markdown → HTML via `markdown2` if installed,
   plain otherwise), and sends via Gmail SMTP_SSL:465. Reuses the pattern
   from `scripts/send_summary_email.py` but parameterized so we don't
   proliferate a 12th sprint-specific send script.
3. **Preflight check.** The script exits with a clear `EmailNotConfigured`
   error if `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` is unset, rather than silently no-opping
   (the failure mode that made `EmailNotifier` dangerous).
4. **Send a test email.** A short markdown `EMAIL_TEST_2026-04-18.md`
   saying "Email delivery confirmed. Reply with 'ack' to this email to
   confirm the inbound side of the CMD-email pattern described in
   `scripts/send_phone_instructions.py`." Delivers to
   `manderson240@gmail.com`.
5. **User confirms receipt.** The user replies in the Claude session
   (or by email) that the test arrived; only then do we proceed to Step 1.

**Decision gate:** email must arrive at `manderson240@gmail.com` within
~60 seconds. If it doesn't:
- Gmail's "Less secure apps" setting is not the cause (App Passwords bypass
  it); check the App Password was typed without spaces being stripped.
- If it still fails, we fall back to **file-only handoffs** (the
  `*_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md` pattern that already worked for `BIOS_RESUME_INSTRUCTIONS.md`)
  and the user picks them up by checking the worktree directory. Steps
  1–5 below still work — they just don't page the user proactively.

**Deliverable:** a working `scripts/send_handoff.py` with a successful
round-trip test, or an explicit "email unavailable → file-only" decision
recorded in `HARDWARE_PROFILE_PRIME.md`.
